synthesis.chosen:
Synthesis, built mainly on design 3. The asset plane writes each asset to an engine-owned AssetStore at `<journal file name>.assets` beside the journal, outside the engine lock, before any acknowledgement. The engine refuses to record bytes its store does not hold. On restore, every journaled scene's declared hashes are read back and re-hashed before preparation. A scene with a missing, altered or unreadable asset is dropped by name: removed from published, and cleared from program/cued if they point at it. The engine still starts at epoch+1, output-inhibited. Drops are named on stderr at start, and through an in-memory refusal on Cue, Take or Render of the dropped take (design 2's refusal-by-reason, without its revision floor, Degradation or pruning). Journal schema stays 3. A store failure is refused with a new Refusal::AssetStoreFailed. No new crate.

Why not each design whole:
- **Design 1** writes under the engine mutex. That breaks ADR-001 ("A 400MB transfer must never be able to delay a cue", Shared/asset-plane/src/lib.rs:3-4) and 5.8's stated property (publish.rs:398-399). It reuses TransportFailed, which the audit defines as client-side only (refusal_audit.rs:2021-2023), against invariant 17 (docs/invariants.md:49). Its with_extension("assets") name equals the journal path for a journal named x.assets.
- **Design 2** gets the lock right but adds start-time pruning (it deletes files, including in the user's real store through the host tests), a Degradation contract change and a revision floor. None of these is needed by the done-when.
- **Design 3** gets the core right but adds a drop-report file format, reparse-point opening, a .gxtmp sweep and a store_bytes link change. All four are extra surface the done-when does not need.
synthesis.plan:
Judgement against the four criteria (all citations verified by reading):
(1) Done-when. Every design meets it only if restore re-hashes every declared asset, images included. Validation needs only the hash (Shared/contracts/src/validate.rs:87). Preparation reads bytes only for fonts and meshes (prepared.rs:138-139; text.rs:471-473). Each design also has to remove a dropped take from `published`. Otherwise ensure_program_backend's identifier-only bypass accepts a Take of it (engine.rs:477-482), and validate() then refuses program/cued pointing at it, which exits the worker 1 (recovery.rs:129-142; main.rs:125-128).
(2) Rules. Write outside the lock (ADR-001), and name a store failure by its own variant (invariant 17). Never read a package path on restore. Schema 3, so a 5.9-era journal starts instead of exiting. Boundary R2 is Editor-only (tools/check-boundaries.mjs:65-72, 341-346). No crate is added: the worker already depends on gx-asset-plane and gx-fs.
(3) Crash consistency. Asset rename, then accept, then publish, then journal write (engine.rs:441). The journal can never name a scene whose bytes were not renamed into the store first. A kill at any point leaves at worst an orphan store file or a .gxtmp.
(4) Blast radius. Only design 3's core plus a ~20-line tombstone. No Status or Degradation change, no prune, no drop-report file.

Steps:
1. **contracts** (Shared/contracts/src/lib.rs):
   - Add `Refusal::AssetStoreFailed { hash: ContentHash, detail: String }` beside AssetHashMismatch (~604), with its Display (~1274), all_variants (1666) and code_name "assetStoreFailed" (2277+).
   - Add `pub fn ContentHash::is_sha256(&self) -> bool` (64 lowercase hex). Shared/contracts/src/package.rs:126-131 and worker main.rs:249 delegate to it (invariant 27).
   - Run `npm run codegen` (Refusal.ts and capability-surface.ts, never hand-edited).
   - Add a refusal-audit Limitation for AssetStoreFailed (list at conformance/src/refusal_audit.rs:2010).
2. **asset-plane store** (Shared/asset-plane/src/store.rs):
   - `read_verified(&self, &ContentHash) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AssetStoreError>`: shape check, one fs::read, then re-hash. A bad shape or NotFound gives Refusal(AssetMissing). Any other I/O error gives ReadCache. A wrong digest gives Refusal(AssetHashMismatch{expected, actual}).
   - `holds_entry(&self, hash, len: u64) -> bool`: shape check, then symlink_metadata must be a regular file of exactly that length.
   - `AssetStoreError::into_refusal(self, &ContentHash) -> Refusal`: Refusal(r) becomes r; everything else becomes AssetStoreFailed{hash, detail: self.to_string()}.

synthesis.store:
The store is `gx_asset_plane::AssetStore::at_root(journal.asset_store_directory())` (store.rs:148-153), with the unchanged production layout: one flat directory, one file per asset named by its 64-hex lowercase SHA-256, no extension (store.rs:228-230). The write path is unchanged: hash in memory, gx_fs::write_atomic_with (temp in the same directory with create_new, sync_all, close, rename with retry), then a post-rename re-hash (store.rs:239-305). An existing file that no longer verifies is overwritten, so a re-upload heals it (store.rs:269-294).

**Directory.** The journal's file name with ".assets" appended, as a sibling, derived only by RecoveryJournal::asset_store_directory():
- production: %APPDATA%\GrapiX\GrapiX\data\render-engine\recovery.json.assets\<hash>, about 145 characters (about 160 for a temp), under MAX_PATH;
- conformance: <scratch>\recovery.json.assets;
- each %TEMP% unit or GPU test journal gets its own <name>.json.assets (engine.rs:1455-1458; gpu_tests.rs:374-381);
- the Editor shell test's own store at scratch/assets (Editor/shell/tests/publish.rs:171) stays separate from the worker's scratch/recovery.json.assets.

Appending, unlike with_extension, can never equal the journal path. open_at refuses a path with no file name.

**Not AssetStore::new().** That is the Editor's cache, which the platform module calls expendable (store.rs:143-145; Shared/contracts/src/platform.rs:95).

**Ownership.** The engine holds the store as Option<Arc<AssetStore>>; promote_verified takes &self (store.rs:239), so no lock is needed.

**New AssetStore methods**: read_verified, holds_entry, AssetStoreError::into_refusal. The shape check uses the new ContentHash::is_sha256, because ContentHash is an unchecked String (contracts lib.rs:82) and cache_path joins it unchecked (store.rs:228-230).

**Location rule.** The done-when's "beside its recovery journal" puts it in Roaming AppData next to the journal.
synthesis.write_path:
Bytes are written by the asset plane, OUTSIDE the engine mutex, before the peer ever receives them. The engine then refuses to record bytes its store does not hold. This makes "accepted ⇒ stored" an engine-side invariant, and both acknowledgements wait on it.

**Why outside the lock.** PeerAssets locks the peer for the whole accept (publish.rs:122-128). deliver_packaged runs under locked() (401). The render loop locks the same Arc<Mutex<Engine>> every frame (main.rs:206-219). A fsync'd write plus re-read hash of a large asset under that lock would delay Program and cues, against ADR-001 (asset-plane lib.rs:3-4).

1. **Trait** (publish.rs:80-108): add the default method `fn asset_store(&self) -> Option<Arc<AssetStore>> { None }`. Engine returns its field. The mock and handoff/publish test peers keep None, so behaviour is unchanged.
2. **Chunked route.** handle_connection reads asset_store() under a brief lock and gives it to PeerAssets.
   1. PeerAssets::accept calls store.promote_verified(hash, &bytes) unlocked. The hash was already verified by the dialect (preflight.rs:441-444).
   2. On Err it returns Ok(Err(e.into_refusal(hash))), which becomes AssetTransferReply::Refused{cause} (preflight.rs:445-447) and never an aborted connection.
   3. Only then does it lock and call accept_verified_asset.
   `Stored{hash}` is written only after accept returns Ok (preflight.rs:446). publish_scene is a later request.
3. **By-path route.**
   1. Read package_directory() and asset_store() under one brief lock.
   2. open_package_in reads and re-hashes unlocked, as today (publish.rs:400).
   3. Promote every packaged asset unlocked. store_bytes skips a file that already verifies (store.rs:269-271). Any Err gives PublishReply::Refused(PackageRefused{cause: AssetStoreFailed..}) before deliver_packaged.
   4. Otherwise deliver_packaged runs under the lock exactly as today (441-454). The Published header is written after it (404), and only after Engine::publish has journaled (engine.rs:441).
4. **Engine** (engine.rs:860-867):
   - accept_verified_asset with no store refuses AssetStoreFailed{hash, "no recovery journal is attached, so this engine has no asset store"}. The worker binary always attaches one (main.rs:114-128), and no in-process engine accepts assets today (only the four test modules call record_verified_asset_bytes).
   - With a store but !holds_entry(hash, len), it refuses AssetStoreFailed{hash, "verified bytes were not written to the engine's asset store before receipt"}.
   - In both refusals nothing changes and output_inhibited is NOT set: memory and disk still agree, unlike the journal-failure case at engine.rs:441-447.
   - has_verified_asset also requires holds_entry. A store entry deleted while the engine runs is then reported missing, re-sent and healed.
5. **Tidy-ups.** Delete the uncalled hash-only record_verified_asset (501-503), which could make `assets` disagree with `asset_bytes`. record_verified_asset_bytes becomes #[cfg(test)] pub(crate).

**Crash windows.**
- Kill during the temp write: only a .gxtmp is left, harmless to lookups.
- Kill after the rename, before accept or the journal write: an unreferenced file. A re-upload skips the rewrite.
- Journal write fails after the store write: the existing refusal plus inhibit (engine.rs:441-447), and an orphan file.
- Power loss: Windows directory fsync is a no-op (Shared/fs/src/atomic.rs:394-402). If NTFS loses the asset rename but keeps the journal, restore drops the scene by name. It never substitutes.
synthesis.restore_path:
**attach_recovery_journal(journal) -> Result<Vec<DroppedScene>, RecoveryError>** (engine.rs:198-210):
1. `let store = Arc::new(AssetStore::at_root(journal.asset_store_directory()))`. This does no I/O.
2. If journal.load()? is Some(state): `dropped = self.restore_state(state, &store)?`, then output_inhibited = true and both rasterisers cleared. This happens UNCONDITIONALLY whenever a journal existed, including when every scene drops (3.12).
3. `self.asset_store = Some(store); self.recovery = Some(journal); self.persist_recovery()?`. This rewrites the journal without the dropped takes before any server binds (main.rs:150).
4. `Ok(dropped)`.

Journal-level faults stay fatal, as today: read/decode, schema, contradictory records, EpochExhausted (recovery.rs:77-154, 286-316).

**restore_state(state, &AssetStore) -> Result<Vec<DroppedScene>, RecoveryError>** (rewrite of 256-305):
1. `state.validate()?` and `state.next_epoch()?`, unchanged.
2. **Read back.** For every PreparedSceneRecord, for every declared `assets[].checksum` of any kind (images included), fill a per-hash verdict cache `HashMap<ContentHash, Result<(), Refusal>>`:
   - `store.read_verified(h)` gives Ok(bytes): insert into a local asset_bytes;
   - Err(e) gives `Err(e.into_refusal(h))`.
   Each hash is read once. Every scene declaring a shared bad hash gets the same cause.
3. **Hashes not loaded.** state.verified_assets is no longer trusted as the available set; line 259 was the root cause. Hashes in it that no journaled scene declares are not loaded. A publisher's preflight reports them missing and re-sends them.
4. **Drop.** For each record, in journal order (sorted by take and revision at engine.rs:231-233), the first failing declared hash, in declaration order, drops the scene before any preparation (see drop_semantics).
5. **Prepare.** Otherwise run the existing PreparedScene::prepare_for_gpu(document, &assets, &asset_bytes, &support), the animation refusal and, on hardware, GpuScene::prepare (264-291). `assets` = asset_bytes.keys(). A failure here, on bytes that verified, keeps today's fatal InvalidState (see decisions).
6. **Commit**, all at once as today (293-304):
   - clock free-running at next_epoch;
   - published minus dropped takes; prepared; gpu_prepared;
   - assets = exactly the hashes read back and verified;
   - asset_bytes = their bytes (NEW; at HEAD it was never restored);
   - cued and program, with drop references cleared;
   - self.dropped = tombstones.

Bytes are needed only during preparation (prepared.rs:104-180), so the GPU and CPU paths rebuild unchanged. The package file and --package-dir are never consulted.

**main.rs** prints the drops on stderr (see reason_surface).

**Schema**: RECOVERY_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 3.
synthesis.drop_semantics:
A journaled scene is dropped if and only if reading back one of its declared content hashes fails. The reason is that Refusal:
- AssetMissing{hash}: no entry, or a hash that is not SHA-256;
- AssetHashMismatch{expected, actual}: altered or truncated bytes;
- AssetStoreFailed{hash, detail}: any other I/O error.

**What a drop does**, before anything is installed:
- (a) `published.remove(take)`. This closes the identifier-only bypass at engine.rs:477-482, through which a Take would otherwise succeed and draw the diagnostic take key after re-arm (306-328).
- (b) `program = None` and `cued = None` ONLY if they name that take. Program or cued on an intact scene survives. Without this, attach's persist fails validate (recovery.rs:129-142) and the worker exits 1.
- (c) No prepared or gpu_prepared entry.
- (d) An in-memory tombstone `dropped[take] = DroppedScene`.

**Tombstone.** While the take is unpublished, Cue and Take (check_published, engine.rs:799-806) and Render (handle_detached, 1081) are refused with the drop reason itself, ahead of UnknownTake, on every tier. A successful re-publish of that take id clears the tombstone. Tombstones are not journaled; after a second restart the take is plain UnknownTake.

**Revision reuse.** A re-publish restarts at Revision(1) (engine.rs:399-404). That is safe: takes pin the content hash (RevisionHashMismatch), and epoch reconciliation already allows a reused revision (mocks/mock-engine/src/lib.rs:212-218).

**Granularity.**
- A scene with one intact and one bad asset is dropped; its intact bytes stay loaded (verified, harmless).
- Scenes sharing a bad hash all drop with the same cause, because there is one file per hash.
- Scenes without assets and identifier-only published entries are kept.

**What a drop never does.** It never prevents start-up. The engine binds, answers at journal epoch+1, and stays output-inhibited until ConfigureOutput. ConfigureOutput re-checks a surviving Program (engine.rs:834-846); a cleared Program re-arms to black (306-310).

**Durability.** The immediate persist makes the drop durable: the journal no longer lists the take, its scene or the hashes of its failing assets.

**Repair.** Re-publish. Preflight reports the failing hash missing, and promote_verified overwrites the altered entry (store.rs:269-294).

**Store files stay.** Removed or altered store files are not deleted (no garbage collection in 5.11).
synthesis.reason_surface:
There is no wire-contract change for drops. There are three surfaces.

**(1) Worker stderr at the start that drops.** It is printed by main.rs after attach returns Ok and before the banner and Server::bind (main.rs:125-150):
- a header `recovery: N journaled scene(s) dropped at epoch E; re-publish them`;
- one line per scene, capped at 8: `recovery: dropped scene conformance/restart-removed/1 (pin <h>): assetMissing: asset missing: <png hash>; it was cued, now clear`;
- then `recovery: and K more`.

The cap exists because gx-engine-host pipes the worker's stdout and stderr and drains them only when the child fails to answer (host/src/lib.rs:163-207). An undrained Windows pipe holds only about 4 KB (not verified), and a blocked eprintln before bind would look like a failed start. Conformance already captures stderr in scratch/stderr.log (conformance/src/main.rs:421-440). stderr is unbuffered and the line is written before the control port binds, so it is on disk by the time start_worker connects.

**(2) Over the wire.** Cue, Take or Render of a dropped take is Refused with the drop reason itself (AssetMissing{h} / AssetHashMismatch{expected, actual} / AssetStoreFailed{h, detail}), so an operator on the host route, where stderr is lost, still sees why. The new epoch in Capability and Status (engine.rs:884, 921) tells a reconciling client to re-check.

**(3) In process.** Engine::dropped_scenes(), and the Vec returned by attach, for unit tests.

**Store-write failures** reach the publisher by name, with no inhibit:
- chunked: AssetTransferReply::Refused{cause: AssetStoreFailed}, which publish_package surfaces as PackagePublishError::Transfer(Refused(..));
- by path: PublishReply::Refused(PackageRefused{cause: AssetStoreFailed});
- an engine without a journal: AssetStoreFailed.

**New variant.** AssetStoreFailed is new and required, because TransportFailed is registered as "a client-side transport failure, not an engine decision" (refusal_audit.rs:2021-2023) and invariant 17 requires the condition by name (docs/invariants.md:49). It needs a TS regen and an audit Limitation; the 5.11 conformance suite drives it against a real worker.

**Cosmetic.** The AssetHashMismatch Display says "transferred bytes" (contracts lib.rs:1274-1277). The stderr line prefixes it with the drop context and the code name.
synthesis.journal_schema:
Unchanged.
- RECOVERY_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 3 (recovery.rs:28).
- RecoveryState and PreparedSceneRecord are byte-identical, so deny_unknown_fields (39, 49) is untouched.
- The bytes live in the sibling store, not in the journal.
- The doc comment records why 3 is kept. A schema-3 journal written by a 5.9 worker, which names asset-bearing scenes but has no store, now starts with those scenes dropped AssetMissing by name. Today such a journal exits 1 with "prepared scene .. cannot be rebuilt: asset missing". A bump to 4 would turn that into UnsupportedSchema, so the worker would still refuse to start.

**Meaning of verifiedAssets tightens** (doc at recovery.rs:57): hashes whose verified bytes are in `<journal>.assets`, meaning accepted since start plus those read back at restore. Restore never trusts the list; it re-reads every journaled scene's declared assets.

**Tombstones are not journaled.**

**Observed on this machine.** The live platform journal (%APPDATA%\GrapiX\GrapiX\data\render-engine\recovery.json, 3 Oct) is schemaVersion 1. It is refused UnsupportedSchema before and after 5.11 and is not auto-discarded; the runbook's rename procedure applies.

**Runbook.** docs/engine-recovery-runbook.md:24 ("Only version 1 is understood") and :28 (verifiedAssets) need updating.

decisions_for_user.question: When a journaled scene's bytes verify but preparation or the GPU still refuses it at restore (a software or capability change, or a transient GPU fault), should the engine drop that scene by name too, or keep today's refusal to start? The done-when covers only missing or altered bytes.
options: Keep refusing to start for these (HEAD behaviour, engine.rs:270-288). The journal stays untouched, so a transient GPU fault cannot erase scenes through the immediate rewrite at engine.rs:209.
Drop these by name as well, so a scene that cannot be rebuilt never keeps the engine down.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Keep refusing to start in 5.11, which matches the done-when literally. If 'never refuse for any bad scene' is wanted, it is a later one-line policy change.

decisions_for_user.question: Should 5.11 garbage-collect the engine store? Today it only grows: files of dropped scenes, altered files and hashes no scene uses stay until a re-upload overwrites them. AssetStore has no delete (store.rs:141-306).
options: No collection in 5.11; file a follow-up row.
Prune at each start to the restored scenes' hashes, after the journal is persisted (design 2). Host tests would then also prune the user's real store.
decisions_for_user.recommendation: No collection in 5.11; file a follow-up row.

decisions_for_user.question: gx-engine-host discards the worker's stderr on success (host/src/lib.rs:163-207), so on the host route the start-time drop lines are lost. The only trace there is the in-memory refusal by reason, which a second restart forgets. Should a durable operator surface be added?
options: Ship 5.11 with stderr plus the refusal by reason; add a follow-up row for a Status or Degradation signal and for the host draining stderr.
Add a Degradation variant or EngineStatus field now (contract and TS change; Degradation is Copy, status.rs:21-32).
Write a drop report file beside the journal before it is rewritten (design 3; a new file format).
decisions_for_user.recommendation: Ship with stderr plus the refusal by reason, and file the follow-up row.

risks: Pre-existing, found while verifying; out of scope, needs its own row. Re-publishing a take while an older revision of it is on Program always fails. publish() moves published to N+1 (engine.rs:432-440), then persist_recovery's validate refuses program N (recovery.rs:129-142). The publish is refused TransportFailed 'recovery journal write failed' AND output is inhibited (engine.rs:441-447). 5.11's tests are designed never to re-publish a take that is on Program; 5.10's frequent Editor publishes would hit it.

Pre-existing: publish() changes prepared and published before the journal write, so a refused publish leaves a takeable revision in memory, contradicting publish.rs:48. 5.11 adds no write inside publish() and leaves this unchanged.

Restore time. Every declared asset is read and re-hashed before the control port binds. gx-engine-host waits 10 s and kills a worker that is running but unreachable (host/src/lib.rs:172-195), so a multi-GB store, or SHA-256 in a debug build, could become a restart loop. The fixtures are about 0.8 MB, within conformance's 15 s deadline. Measure release-build throughput in a follow-up.

Any read error that is not NotFound (for example a Defender sharing violation at startup) drops the scene as AssetStoreFailed with no retry. The journal is rewritten at attach, so the drop is durable; recovery is a re-publish. A bounded retry like gx_fs's rename_retrying (Shared/fs/src/atomic.rs:340-373) is optional hardening.

Drop names on the host route: see the decision. The stderr cap (8 lines) keeps the undrained pipe from filling before bind. The pipe size (about 4 KB) was not verified. The render loop's per-frame eprintln on emission failure (main.rs:222) is an existing way to fill it.
Output inhibition cannot be observed over the wire on these free-running workers: live_allowed is false either way (engine.rs:927, 780-788). It is proved only by the in-process unit asserts.

Host integration tests start workers on the user's real platform journal (services/render-engine/host/tests/ensure.rs:88-99). That journal is schemaVersion 1, observed on this machine, so those workers exit UnsupportedSchema before and after 5.11. If it is ever replaced, the tests will write recovery.json.assets into the user's real data directory.
The store sits in Roaming AppData beside the journal, as the done-when requires (platform.rs:87-93), so a roaming profile would sync large assets.

A kill mid-write leaves a .<name>.<pid>.<seq>.<nanos>.gxtmp (atomic.rs:315-333) that nothing sweeps; lookups ignore it. Conformance's remove and alter steps must target the 64-hex file, and should retry on OS errors 32/33 in case Defender holds a just-written file.

has_verified_asset and the accept guard only stat the file. A store file altered at runtime with the same length goes unnoticed until the next restart, which then drops its scene by name; memory still serves the correct bytes until then.
The new trait hook widens AssetPublishPeer. A future peer that forgets to return its store gets 5.9's memory-only behaviour; only the engine's guard enforces 'accepted implies stored'.
Invariant 27 parity: the mock engine stays memory-only with no journal (mocks/mock-engine/src/lib.rs:339-352). 5.11 is engine-only; the evidence says so.
The standalone AssetTransferServer still turns a store error into an io::Error that aborts the connection (preflight.rs:325-331). Left unchanged in 5.11; into_refusal makes it a one-line fix later.
The conformance real-engine scratch from run_against_real_engine is never removed, so each run now also leaks the stored font and PNG (about 0.8 MB) in %TEMP%.
Fresh ports per restart, so Client::reconnect's epoch reconciliation across a real kill is not exercised.
Keep run 2 and the unwritable-store check independent of run 1's outcome. Each uses its own worker and needs only a successful start.

gaps.gap: A restarted worker that never answers is recorded as a SKIP, which hides the exact failure 5.11 exists to catch (S1 "still starts", R2 "restarts on its journal").
gaps.evidence: The plan maps restart failures "as 509-512": Exited becomes fail_to_start and Unavailable becomes skip_unavailable (conformance/src/main.rs:509-512). start_worker returns Unavailable when the port never answers within 15 s (main.rs:443, 458-463). StartFailure::Unavailable is documented as "the peer is unavailable, a skip" (main.rs:397-403), and skip_unavailable records a Skip (conformance/src/lib.rs:150-156). A restore that hangs or runs past 15 s (for example a slow re-hash, or a blocked write before Server::bind at worker main.rs:150) would therefore be a SKIP. Invariant 47 (docs/invariants.md:136-139) says a check that always skips is not a check.
gaps.fix: In kill_and_restart, treat both Exited and Unavailable as fail_to_start (FAIL), with the stderr.log text in the message. The same binary with the same flags has already answered once in this run, so failing to answer after a restart is the defect, not an unavailable peer. Keep skip_unavailable only for the first start of each worker. Add a mutation (sleep 20 s in restore_state) that must show FAIL, not SKIP.

gaps.gap: R4 accepts Taken on any tier, and R3/S4 can compare None with None. A scene that was not restored but stayed published can still pass, or skip, the take check.
gaps.evidence: ensure_program_backend returns Ok for any published revision that has no prepared scene (engine.rs:477-482). A sub-T0 device never has hardware: gpu.rs:80-81 returns inner None for !live_capable, and has_hardware() is inner.is_some() (gpu.rs:143-145). So below T0, Taken can only come from the identifier-only bypass, never from a restored prepared revision (that is refused TierTooLow, engine.rs:487-490). The plan copies asset_route's pattern, where Taken is Pass on every tier (asset_route.rs:458). package_handoff::render returns None on any non-Rendered reply (package_handoff.rs:90-112). 5.8 had to add `a.is_some()` explicitly (package_handoff.rs:224-229), but the plan's R3 and S4 only say "equal RenderedFrame".
gaps.fix: R4/S4: read cap.device_tier. On T0 only Taken passes. Below T0 only Refused(TierTooLow) is a named SKIP, and Taken is a FAIL ("a prepared revision cannot be taken below T0; the take used the identifier-only path, so the scene was not restored"). Run R3 before R4. R3/S4: require that both renders are Some, that the fetched image bytes are equal, and that the image hash is unchanged.

gaps.gap: The 8-line stderr cap, plus printing after the journal rewrite, means some dropped scenes are never named anywhere durable. That contradicts "dropped with a named reason".
gaps.evidence: The plan prints at most 8 `dropped scene` lines, then `and K more`. Those lines are printed in main after attach returns (worker main.rs:125-130). attach has already rewritten the journal without the dropped takes (engine.rs:209, persist_recovery inside attach). Tombstones live in memory only and are forgotten at the next restart. On the production route, gx-engine-host pipes stderr and reads it only when the child fails to answer (host/src/lib.rs:163-207). So scene 9 and later get no name at all, and a kill between the persist and the eprintln loses every name.
gaps.fix: Make the full drop list durable before the journal is rewritten. For example, have attach atomically write `<journal file name>.dropped.json` (all DroppedScene records, epoch) via gx_fs::write_atomic before persist_recovery. Then print to stderr with a byte budget rather than a line count, and point to that file. Alternatively, return the drops from restore, print them before persisting, and have the host drain stderr. Add a unit test with 9 or more drops that asserts every take id is named, and a test that the report exists even if the process stops right after persist.

gaps.gap: AssetStoreFailed{detail: AssetStoreError::to_string()} sends the engine's filesystem path (which contains the Windows user name) to remote publishers, and through the tombstone to Playout. 5.8's review removed exactly this kind of leak.
gaps.evidence: Every non-Refusal AssetStoreError Display embeds path.display() (Shared/asset-plane/src/store.rs:61-90: CreateCacheDirectory, WriteCache, ReadCache, CacheHashMismatch). The production store is %APPDATA%\GrapiX\GrapiX\data\render-engine\recovery.json.assets (worker recovery.rs:31, host lib.rs:68-72). docs/evidence/5.8/review-2026-11-08.md:17, finding 4: "PackageUnreadable's detail repeated the engine's link-resolved path ... The detail carries only the cause." The chunked refusal reaches a LAN client (preflight.rs:445-447). The plan's tombstone returns the same Refusal on Cue, Take and Render.
gaps.fix: Build the detail in into_refusal from the operation and the io::Error kind/raw OS code only, for example "store write failed: Access is denied (os error 5)". Never include a path. The hash already identifies the entry. Print the full path only on the worker's stderr. Add a unit test, and an assertion in the conformance unwritable-store check, that the detail contains neither the scratch path nor "recovery.json.assets".

gaps.gap: The planned lock-independence test signals from has_verified_asset on the chunked route. The dialect calls has() twice, so holding the peer mutex after the first signal blocks Begin. A correct implementation would then FAIL (time out).
gaps.evidence: AssetTransferClient::publish sends Preflight, then transfer() sends Begin, then Chunks (preflight.rs:222-242, 171-186). The server calls assets.has() for Preflight (preflight.rs:380-386) and again for Begin (preflight.rs:390-394), and each call locks the peer (publish.rs:116-121). If the test takes the mutex after the Preflight-time has(), Begin's has() blocks. No chunk arrives, so promote_verified never runs, and the store file cannot appear before release.
gaps.fix: Have the test peer count has_verified_asset calls and signal on the Begin call (the second call for a one-asset publish). Or drive the dialect by hand: send Preflight and Begin, take the mutex, then send the chunks. Then assert the store file appears while the mutex is held and that Stored arrives after release. The package-route variant (signal from package_directory()) is fine as planned.

gaps.gap: The refusal-audit limitations become false, and mock parity (invariant 45) is not addressed for the new engine-only refusals.
gaps.evidence: Today's limitation reads `AssetMissing`: "asset publication has no EnginePeer request" (conformance/src/refusal_audit.rs:2012-2014). The planned AssetStoreFailed limitation repeats that claim. But the plan's tombstone makes Cue/Take (check_published, engine.rs:799-806) and Render (handle_detached, engine.rs:1077-1099), all EnginePeer requests, return AssetMissing, AssetHashMismatch or AssetStoreFailed. Invariant 45 (docs/invariants.md:130-132): "A mock peer must refuse exactly where the real engine refuses." The mock's accept and has are documented as "the same receipt as the engine's" (mocks/mock-engine/src/lib.rs:339-352). After the plan, the engine refuses where the mock accepts (no store, store write failure, and holds_entry false).
gaps.fix: Drive AssetMissing and AssetStoreFailed in the refusal audit through EnginePeer. The audit already builds an in-process Engine (refusal_audit/drawability.rs:36): attach a journal whose store lacks, or cannot read, a declared asset, restart, and Take or Render the dropped take. Then move both variants to is_driven and delete or reword the limitations. Update the mock's "same receipt" comment, and add an evidence note (or a mock test) stating why parity holds: the mock never restores from a journal. Otherwise give the mock the same guard.

gaps.gap: read_verified reads a whole store entry into memory with no size bound. An altered entry that grew, which is one form of the done-when's "altered", can delay or crash restore before the control port binds. That is "refusing to start" by another route.
gaps.evidence: The plan's read_verified does "one fs::read" and then re-hashes. Restore runs before Server::bind (worker main.rs:125, 150). The host kills a worker that has not answered within 10 s and retries (host/src/lib.rs:172-195). The 5.8 review fixed exactly this class (memory.md: read_package "no longer reserves the zip's declared size (a crafted package aborted the engine ...)"; reads bounded by the manifest length + 1). The plan's damage tests cover only a same-length byte flip and a half-truncation.
gaps.fix: In read_verified, take symlink_metadata first. Refuse without reading any entry whose length exceeds a bound: the declared size_bytes when the document carries it, otherwise MAX_PACKAGE_BYTES (Shared/asset-plane/src/package.rs:47). Name it AssetHashMismatch, or AssetStoreFailed with "entry is N bytes". Then read with a reader limited to len+1. Add a unit test with a sparse or large grown entry that drops by name in milliseconds, and add a grown-file case to the conformance damage run.

gaps.gap: Invariant 27: the plan adds a third read-and-rehash implementation and leaves the two Editor copies unchanged, and their behaviour differs.
gaps.evidence: Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:282-290 (scene_asset_bytes: no 64-hex shape check, so a document checksum is joined into a path; any I/O error becomes AssetMissing). Editor/shell/src/lib.rs:823-842 (cmd_font_bytes: shape check, any error becomes AssetMissing). The planned AssetStore::read_verified maps non-NotFound errors to AssetStoreFailed and adds the shape check. files_touched omits Editor/shell/src/lib.rs. docs/invariants.md:72-73: parallel implementations must change together.
gaps.fix: Route both Editor call sites through AssetStore::read_verified in the same commit, mapping its error with into_refusal, and add Editor/shell/src/lib.rs to files_touched. Or record a named exemption with its reason in the 5.11 evidence.

gaps.gap: publish() acknowledges a scene against the in-memory `assets` set, never the store. A store entry deleted or replaced while the engine runs still yields Published, and that scene is then lost at the next restart.
gaps.evidence: publish() validates with &self.assets and &self.asset_bytes (engine.rs:406-411) and replies Published after the journal write (engine.rs:441-453). The plan adds holds_entry only to has_verified_asset and accept_verified_asset, not to publish(). The done-when requires the bytes to be in the store "before the publication is acknowledged".
gaps.fix: In publish(), after preparation succeeds and before the journal write, check store.holds_entry(hash, asset_bytes[hash].len()) for every declared checksum. If an entry is missing, return PreparationRefused{AssetMissing{hash}} and change nothing. Add a test: delete the store entry, publish, get AssetMissing; re-upload repairs it.

gaps.gap: Conformance R1 finds the store by calling the derivation under test, so M19's claim that "R1's file check FAILs" is wrong for a mutation of asset_store_directory itself.
gaps.evidence: The plan's R1 checks `RecoveryJournal::open_at(journal).asset_store_directory()/3127f0b8...`. If asset_store_directory() is changed to `<parent>/assets`, the engine and the check move together and R1 still passes. Only the unit test the_store_is_named_after_its_journal_file would fail. The done-when says the store is "beside its recovery journal".
gaps.fix: In R1, also assert the location independently: the file exists at `scratch.join("recovery.json.assets").join(hash)`, and asset_store_directory().parent() == journal.parent(). Correct the M19 row so it names the unit test as the failing check for that mutation variant.

gaps.gap: Reusing a revision number after a drop is justified only by the mock's docs, not by invariants 30 and 61, and a cheap floor is available.
gaps.evidence: publish() numbers from `published` only (engine.rs:399-404), so a dropped take that is published again gets Revision(1), even if the dropped revision was 1 with different content. docs/invariants.md:82-84 ("Every publish is a new version") and 196-199 ("a version number identifies a publish"). The plan's tombstone already holds the dropped revision.
gaps.fix: In publish(), compute the next revision as max(published revision, tombstone revision) + 1, so numbers are not reused within the incarnation. Durable reuse protection (a journaled revision floor) is left to the user as a decision. Add a unit test: the take is dropped at Revision(3), and publishing it again yields Revision(4).
